findings.evidence: "Similarly, the people operations office updates the equipment catalog each quarter."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with "Also" or "Additionally," or restructure as a separate paragraph.
findings.violation: The transition word "Similarly" is incorrect. The previous sentence discusses budget tracking, while this sentence discusses catalog updates - these are not parallel processes, and the frequencies differ (fiscal year vs. quarterly).

findings.evidence: "The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition and this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Separate into two sentences: "The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition. This office may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: Two independent clauses are awkwardly joined with "and" without proper punctuation or conjunction.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break this into multiple shorter sentences that clearly separate eligibility criteria, conditions, and tracking responsibilities.
findings.violation: This sentence is extremely long and convoluted, with multiple nested clauses that make it nearly incomprehensible.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Also, you submit the request in the portal."
findings.fix: Replace "You record" and "you submit" with "Employees record" and "Employees submit" to maintain consistent voice.
findings.violation: This section shifts to second-person perspective ("you"), which conflicts with the formal, third-person voice used throughout the rest of the document that refers to "employees," "the applicant," and "the team."

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Expand to include all required documentation: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, uploading the receipt, obtaining the manager's approval form, and submitting the original purchase order."
findings.violation: This section lists only eligibility confirmation and receipt upload, but the "How to Apply" section requires three items: receipt, manager's approval form, and original purchase order. The incomplete list contradicts the earlier section.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Delete the Special Cases section entirely, or if it serves a distinct purpose, rewrite it with unique content that does not duplicate Program Overview.
findings.violation: This text is identical to the first section of Program Overview (with "finance liaison" substituted for "benefits team"), creating exact duplication.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Delete this section or rewrite with unique content distinct from Program Overview.
findings.violation: This text duplicates content from Program Overview nearly verbatim.

findings.evidence: Program Overview: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget"; Special Cases: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget"; Questions and Updates: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget"
findings.fix: Clarify whether these are the same entity with different titles, or different entities with different responsibilities. Use consistent naming throughout, or explicitly define roles if multiple departments are involved.
findings.location: Program Overview, Special Cases, and Questions and Updates (cross-document issue)
findings.violation: Three different departments or roles are presented as tracking or reviewing the same budget, creating confusion about responsibility and authority.
